messages.subject: Efficient data transfer for simulation studies
messages.subject_clean: Efficient data transfer for simulation studies
messages.body_plain:
Hello,

I've been using the package to conduct simulation studies for latent classes for a few year now, and it is absolutely wonderful. I wanted to ask if there is a more time-efficient way for me to complete the simulations. Currently, I am writing out data.frames from R to the disk as a ".dat" file using the prepareMplus function, fitting the model(s) in Mplus saving the cprobs (which writes out another.dat file) , and then reading in the results using the readModels function. I notice that a significant amount of computation time is spent writing the files .dat files to the disk, so I'm wondering if there is an alternative way of transferring the data between the programs. Specifically, perhaps there is there a way to keep port the data between the programs in memory rather than having to write to the hard drive?

Thanks so much!

Marcus

messages.subject: Re: Efficient data transfer for simulation studies
messages.subject_clean: Efficient data transfer for simulation studies
messages.body_plain:
Hi Marcus,

To my knowledge there is no workaround for the disk I/O challenge you mention. A shared memory approach between R and Mplus would require low-level access to the memory of either program, or some sort of message passing interface. Both of those would require significant work on the part of R and Mplus developers.

Two thoughts about how to improve this, though:

1) Setup a RAM disk, which basically sets up a filesystem in memory, which should be extremely fast and close to what you want. Use the RAM disk as the target for prepareMplusData and Mplus execution. As long as you don't need a lot of disk space, this should be a good solution.
2) Use a fast SSD/NVM disk as the target, not a platter-based hard drive.

I haven't tried the RAM disk for this application, but the SSD does help substantially in my experience.

Best,
Michael

messages.subject: createModels template usevariables
messages.body_plain:
Hello!

This is likely a fairly simple issue, but I'm having trouble dissecting it from the Vignette examples.

I'm producing multiple data generation files for a number of mixtures.  Therefore, I have various iterators.  Most are fairly simple, however, I'm hung on how to appropriately get MplusAutomation to change the "UseVariables=" values.

For example, I'd like to produce input files that have both a 3 item input, say A1-A3; value and a 5 item input, say A1-A5; value for the UseVariables to loop through.

The problem I keep running into is that the values do not match between the list init variables number and the iterator.

For example:

iterators = sampsize model;
sampsize = 200 500;
model = 1:3
var_set1#model = A1-A3;
var_set2#model = A1-A5;

This is identical to the complete example in the Vignette, except var_set2#model has a different length than the "model" iterator.

I receive this error:
"Variable locked to iterator: model, but has different length."

Is there a work around to loop this through all models with both a 3 item indicator set up and a 5 item indicators set up?

Thank you!

Morgan

messages.subject: Can MplusAutomation extract multinomial logistic regression coefficients following LCA (R3STEP)?
messages.subject_clean: Can MplusAutomation extract multinomial logistic regression coefficients following LCA (R3STEP)?
messages.body_plain:
Does anyone know if MplusAutomation can extract coefficients from the multinomial logistic regressions carried out as part of a LCA model? (using the R3STEP <https://statmodel.com/examples/webnotes/AuxMixture_submitted_corrected_webnote> options)

E.g. the output looks like this:

TESTS OF CATEGORICAL LATENT VARIABLE MULTINOMIAL LOGISTIC REGRESSIONS USING
THE 3-STEP PROCEDURE

                                                    Two-Tailed
                    Estimate       S.E.  Est./S.E.    P-Value

 #1       ON
    AGE               -0.099      0.039     -2.551      0.011
    FEMALE            -0.364      0.178     -2.048      0.041

 #2       ON
    AGE               -0.135      0.047     -2.867      0.004
    FEMALE            -0.346      0.198     -1.751      0.080

 Intercepts
    #1                 1.259      0.419      3.008      0.003
    #2                 2.074      0.502      4.128      0.000

Parameterization using Reference Class 1

[...]

I couldn't find these numbers anywhere the output of readModels. If not, I can go ahead and extract them manually, but thought I'd check first.

Thanks as always, for creating such a useful package!

Ewan

messages.subject: Re: createModels template usevariables
messages.body_plain:
Hi Morgan,

It's been a long time since I wrote that part of the package, but my memory is that it doesn't support the hyphen expansion. Does this work?

model = 1:3;
var_set1#model = A1 A2 A3;
var_set2#model = A1 A2 A3;

Note that your A1-A5 doesn't match the number of models (3).

Michael
